items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: he wrote a couple of minor blues actually, wrote them actually for George Coleman but we never recorded them

ctx.x: When you said, we were talking about people stealing, borrowing, etcetera, other composers, who are the people that you borrowed from on the way up?

Me? Oh I steal from — I don’t borrow from anybody, I steal. I do steal. Bartok. I have a tune, I don’t know if you’re familiar with a record of mine called “The Essence” on DMP with Hank Jones and Billy Higgins. A trio recording. And I wrote a tune, the title tune, “The Essence” is Bartok String Quartet No. 1, it’s the principal theme that opens up the quartet [scats] just those four notes. And I took those very same notes, I didn’t even transpose it, took the very same notes and wrote this tune “The Essence”…
